evals.prompt: Author a production-ready AWS CDK v2 TypeScript stack that provisions an encrypted S3 bucket, a KMS key, and a Lambda function granted read-only access to the bucket, wired with `cdk-nag` (`AwsSolutionsChecks`). Explain the key CDK v2 import and stateful safety rules applied.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill
Uses unified `aws-cdk-lib` and `constructs` imports (never legacy `@aws-cdk/*` v1 packages)
Applies `RemovalPolicy.RETAIN` (or explicit stateful retention), `BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL`, KMS encryption, and L2 grant methods (`bucket.grantRead(fn)`) instead of wildcard IAM policies
Applies `Aspects.of(app).add(new AwsSolutionsChecks())` (or stack-level `cdk-nag`) and recommends verifying with `npx cdk synth` / `npx cdk diff`

evals.prompt: We moved our production `rds.DatabaseCluster` construct inside a new nested `DatabaseConstruct` wrapper in AWS CDK v2, and `cdk diff` now shows `[-] AWS::RDS::DBCluster` and `[+] AWS::RDS::DBCluster` (full database replacement!). Explain why this happens and show the two safe ways (`cdk refactor` vs `overrideLogicalId` / `allocateLogicalId`) to refactor without replacing the database.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill
Explains that CloudFormation logical IDs in CDK are derived from the construct tree path + ID, so reparenting a construct changes its logical ID and triggers replacement
Covers `cdk refactor` (CloudFormation stack refactoring mapping old logical IDs to new paths) and `CfnResource.overrideLogicalId(...)`
Mandates `RemovalPolicy.RETAIN` on stateful database constructs and verifying `cdk diff` shows zero `AWS::RDS::DBCluster` replacements before `cdk deploy`

evals.prompt: Our serverless engineers are waiting 4 minutes per Lambda code change during local CDK dev loops. Compare `cdk deploy --hotswap` (`--hotswap-fallback`), `cdk watch`, and CDK Express / `--method=direct` deployments, and explain why `--hotswap` must never be used in production pipelines.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill

Contrasts `--hotswap` / `--hotswap-fallback` (bypasses CloudFormation Change Sets to update supported resources like Lambda code/Step Functions directly, introducing deliberate CloudFormation drift) against `--method=direct` / standard CloudFormation deployments
Explicitly warns that `--hotswap` is strictly for non-production developer inner loops because it causes CloudFormation stack drift and skips rollback guarantees

evals.prompt: We removed an `s3.Bucket` reference passed from `StorageStack` to `ComputeStack` in CDK v2 and ran `cdk deploy --all`, which failed with `Export StorageStack:ExportsOutputFnGetAtt... cannot be deleted as it is in use by ComputeStack`. Explain why CDK created this deadlock and provide the exact two-phase `exportValue()` fix.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill
Explains that CloudFormation blocks deleting a `Fn::Export` in the producer stack while the deployed consumer stack still imports it via `Fn::ImportValue`

Provides the standard two-deployment decoupling procedure: Phase 1 explicitly retains the export in `StorageStack` via `this.exportValue(...)` while deploying `ComputeStack` without the reference; Phase 2 removes `this.exportValue(...)` from `StorageStack` and deploys cleanly

evals.prompt: We inherited an older CDK v1 TypeScript repo (`@aws-cdk/core`, `@aws-cdk/aws-lambda`, `@aws-cdk/aws-dynamodb` in `package.json` and legacy feature flags in `cdk.json`). Give us the step-by-step migration plan to AWS CDK v2 without causing resource replacements in production.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill
Replaces split `@aws-cdk/*` v1 dependencies with single `aws-cdk-lib` + `constructs` (`^10.x`) packages and updates TypeScript imports accordingly
Warns against enabling breaking `cdk.json` context feature flags during the v1->v2 upgrade if they alter logical IDs or synthesize resource diffs
Requires re-bootstrapping with CDK v2 (`cdk bootstrap` modern template) and validating zero unintended resource replacements via `cdk diff` before deploying

evals.prompt: `npx cdk deploy` in our CI pipeline just failed with: `SSM parameter /cdk-bootstrap/hnb659fds/version not found. Has the environment been bootstrapped?` Even though our landing zone team says they bootstrapped the account with custom qualifier `corpsec`. Diagnose the root cause and fix.
expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill
Identifies the bootstrap qualifier mismatch (`DefaultStackSynthesizer` defaulting to `hnb659fds` while the account was bootstrapped under custom qualifier `corpsec`, or wrong target account/region)
Shows how to configure `@aws-cdk/core:bootstrapQualifier` in `cdk.json` context or pass `DefaultStackSynthesizer({ qualifier: 'corpsec' })` (and verify account/region resolution)
Avoids telling the user to blindly run `AdministratorAccess` `cdk bootstrap` if a landing-zone custom qualifier already exists

expectations: Activates the aws-cdk skill

Flags environment-agnostic stacks (`env` omitted) breaking `Vpc.fromLookup` (`account` and `region` must be explicitly specified on `StackProps.env` and `cdk.context.json` committed for deterministic synth)

Flags passing plaintext `DB_PASSWORD` via `process.env` into CloudFormation template synthesis (which bakes plaintext secrets into synthesized CloudFormation templates/assets) and replaces it with `SecretValue.secretsManager(...)` or `rds.Credentials.fromGeneratedSecret(...)`
